title: RAW an anticipated disclosure consequence motivates an order intended to prevent it
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. The owned pliant-glass story links an exceptional demonstration to a forecast of changed comparative value, then presents an emperor's order as intended to keep the craft unknown. Anticipation, purpose, command and accomplished outcome remain different claims.

source.work: Robert Steele, Mediaeval Lore from Bartholomew Anglicus, selected and modernized historical excerpts
source.owned_unit: Complete edited chapter I MEDIAEVAL SCIENCE, id00045 inclusive through id00109 exclusive, including the final planetary-motion passage. Editorial introduction separately read for provenance.
source.locus: Entire glass paragraph id00107, from glass's properties and reported discovery through ordinary repair, the exceptional vial demonstration, the emperor's order and the conditional comparative-value explanation.
source.source_limit: The anthology selects and modernizes Trevisa material. The anecdote is a narrated historical claim, not verified history, an actual economic study, or a modern recommendation. No independent witness or full medieval-book collation is supplied.

design.working_hypothesis: A written narrative may state an anticipated consequence as the reason for a preventive order while withholding whether either the feared consequence or the prevention actually occurred. Here the craft's possible disclosure and the projected comparative value of nonbrittle glass explain a command meant to suppress knowledge.

connected_relations.input: Ordinary broken glass is said to require remelting; an exceptional maker's vial bends without breaking and is repaired with a hammer.
connected_relations.intermediate: The narrative supplies a contrasting capability, not merely a second material name.

connected_relations.condition: If glass vessels were not brittle, the text says they would be valued above gold vessels; gold and other metals would lose comparative worth.
connected_relations.intermediate: This is an anticipated or conditional valuation, not a reported price change.

connected_relations.purpose: The emperor orders the maker's death lest the craft become known.
connected_relations.consequence: The projected valuation explains the preventive command; the narrated order does not itself establish successful secrecy or completion of the killing.

ownership_and_scope: The maker produces, demonstrates and repairs the vial. The emperor is the issuer of the command. The craft is the object whose disclosure is to be prevented.
The vial bears the demonstrated exceptional property. Glass vessels, gold vessels and metals bear the projected comparative values; those are not properties transferred to the maker.

The text attributes a preventive purpose to the order. It does not identify all knowers of the craft, establish sole possession of the knowledge, prove successful suppression or report an actual market response.
The anecdote presents the motive through its narrator. It does not independently document the emperor's private mental state or verify the story's historicity.
No manufacturing recipe, implementation of coercion or endorsement of the command is proposed. The semantic question concerns the distinction among condition, forecast, purpose and result.
design.distinguishing_consequence: An account claiming that metal values actually fell, that the craft certainly became unknown, or that the order was executed would add outcomes not narrated here. An account reporting only unusual glass would omit the written forecast and the prevention purpose. The same material and actor names cannot settle those modal and intentional differences.

rivals.name: Exceptional-material description only
rivals.account: The story simply describes a repairable vial.
rivals.difference: It omits the comparative-value forecast and the order's stated disclosure-prevention purpose.

rivals.name: Actual consequence report
rivals.account: Nonbrittle glass became widespread and metal values subsequently fell.
rivals.difference: This turns a conditional anticipated outcome into an accomplished event absent from the passage.

rivals.name: Purpose guarantees success
rivals.account: Because the order aims to suppress the craft, the craft is successfully concealed.
rivals.difference: The written intention and command do not report that result, sole knowledge or subsequent history.

rivals.name: Independent complete narrative clauses
rivals.account: A narrative states demonstration, forecast and command separately without reusable semantic composition.
rivals.difference: This remains compatible with the source. Future complete written recurrence would be needed to motivate a reusable construction.
